BEST CORRECTION IN THE BATCH: the DLE gives the locucion adverbial «en silencio» as "Sin protestar, sin quejarse. Sufrir en silencio" — NOT "sin hablar". MISSING-YOU ANGLE: it is not a shortened "I miss you" but a SUBJECTLESS NON-FINITE PARTICIPIAL PHRASE. Evidence from a hostile witness — Crowther, How to Write Letters (1922, PG #22222, read in full) names "the participial closing of a letter", lists its four stock examples, CONDEMNS it, and gives the reason it existed: "A letter used to be considered lacking in ease if it ended with an emphatic sentence." Plus Universal Dependencies v2 (the -ing participle is tagged progressive WITHOUT the auxiliary, so duration sits in the participle, not the am) and an original count of 75 Wollstonecraft love letters 1793-95: 26 Yours-closings, ZERO sentence-initial participial formulae.
